title: Write a task-oriented guide to parallel edges (manual guide + protocol note)
description: Tenant ask (priority 3): expose parallel edges (same predicate, same pair, different provenance), which 'may only mean surfacing the discriminator the format already reserves'. Verified 2026-10-24: shipped in 0.5 (acetone-o8r; PRs #251/#252). Declared discriminators work through schema apply, CREATE/MERGE, reads, import --disc and the report's disc field. The manual's CLI reference documents them (docs/manual/src/reference/cli.md, around lines 264-279), the glossary defines 'discriminator', and CHANGELOG 0.5.0 describes them. The gap is narrower than 'undiscoverable': there is no task-oriented guide, and docs/protocol.md never mentions discriminators.
design: Write a task-oriented 'Parallel relationships' guide in the manual's guide section, linked from docs/user-guide.md. Cross-link the existing reference text rather than duplicating it. Cover: declaring a discriminator with schema apply (and why declare-rel-type deliberately cannot); CREATE/MERGE behaviour (different values coexist; the same value is refused as a duplicate; null or absent is refused); SET/REMOVE of the discriminator refused as an identity change; import --disc; how diff, report and export show the discriminator; and the merge caveat until acetone-7qw.26 lands. In protocol.md, note that edges in rows and in the report carry the discriminator. Exercise every example in a doc test or CLI integration test so the guide cannot rot.
acceptance_criteria: A reader of the manual's guide alone, reached from docs/user-guide.md, can declare, create, query, edit and import parallel edges. Every example is exercised by a test. protocol.md notes the discriminator on edges.

title: Crash between abort_merge's workspace reset and MERGE_HEAD delete leaves a stray MERGE_HEAD; next commit records a merge
description: Found while pinning the abort_merge ref window (acetone-d5is.2, PR #304). If the process dies after the workspace CAS but before MERGE_HEAD is deleted, recovery leaves MERGE_HEAD over a clean workspace, so a following commit records a two-parent merge commit. Pre-existing. Fix: on detecting MERGE_HEAD with a workspace equal to HEAD's tree and no conflicts, treat the merge as aborted (or make commit refuse and point at merge --abort); pin with a test that rebuilds the half-aborted state.
close_reason: Shipped in #312 (squash 7e54d20): abort_merge now marks a fully resolved merge with an empty conflicts map, deletes MERGE_HEAD, then resets the workspace, all under the WriteLock, so a crash at any point leaves a state the next commit completes or a re-run merge --abort finishes; the old-order stray state is still recovered by abort. Deviation from the first design, from review: save_in_place refuses every write while a conflicts map stands with no MERGE_HEAD (naming merge --abort), so a write cannot clear the mark. protocol.md documents that status shows a dirty workspace with no merge block in that window. No format change.

title: Declare-time discriminator gaps: new rel type declared with a discriminator over stored edges; rel-type entry deletion unchecked
description: Surfaced by acetone-7qw.26 (PR #303). (1) check_rel_disc_stability lets a relationship type that is new to the schema be declared with a discriminator over edges already stored under that type (the stability check only compares against a previously declared entry). (2) Deleting a relationship-type entry is not checked against existing edges. Both are declare-time siblings of the merge-time check #303 adds; fix by mirroring the same stale-discriminator rule at declare time.
close_reason: Shipped in #311 (squash 7791d99): check_rel_disc_stability treats an absent rtype entry as declaring no discriminator, so declaring a discriminator for a new type over stored edges, or deleting an entry that declared one, is a change; a change is refused when an edge of that type survives from the old edge map (provenance, as ADR-0082), so a change riding with the deletion of every edge it would falsify lands. Deviation from the first design, from review: rename_rel_type's reconcile step now treats an absent declaration the same way and refuses (RelTypeRenameConflict) a one-sided rename that would put an undeclared side's edges under a declared discriminator, in both directions.

title: Report v2 follow-ups from PR #301 review: docs, comments and violation/schema item tests
description: Non-blocking findings from the PR #301 (acetone-y629) review, to close in Phase 13 (ADR-0054): (1) report v2 renders bytes/temporal base/ours/theirs values through value_to_json ({"$type": ...}), consistent with nodes[].properties but not stated in the CHANGELOG entry or protocol.md's report version history; state it. title: CLI help omits ancestry refspecs (main~1, HEAD^) shipped in #284
description:
Component: the help strings in `crates/acetone-cli/src/cli.rs`. Found in Phase 12 demo step 6.

Since 0.7 (acetone-bvq, #284), git ancestry refspecs (`main~N`, `HEAD^`, `^N`) resolve everywhere a refspec is accepted. Every refspec help string still says only "branch/tag short name, full ref name or commit hash":
- `branch [REFSPEC]` (~l.160)
- `tag [REFSPEC]` (~l.190)
- `diff FROM TO` (l.216)
- `merge REF` (~l.261)
- `schema --at` (l.361/367)
- `query --at` (l.458)

This is the same kind of staleness that #292 fixed in spec §5.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each refspec help string mentions the ancestry syntax.
- The help for `report`, `blame` and `serve`, and the manual, are checked for the same phrase and fixed.

title: Add acetone log --oneline
description:
Component: `acetone log`, and possibly `acetone blame`. Found in Phase 12 demo step 6, where the demo had to fake compact output with `cut`.

`log` has only `--all` and `--json`, so there is no compact form. Users with git habits reach for `--oneline` first.

Design points:
- Interaction with `--all`: should merge commits show their parent hashes?
- Make it mutually exclusive with `--json`.
- Consider the same flag for `blame`.

A candidate for next grooming, not a blocker.
acceptance_criteria:
- `--oneline` prints an abbreviated hash and the subject per commit, with trailers suppressed.
- It is rejected together with `--json`.

title: CLI: workspace discard / restore (checkout refuses even current branch when dirty)
description: PR #178: there is no way to throw away uncommitted workspace changes from the CLI; checkout refuses when dirty even for the current branch. Operators need acetone checkout --discard (or restore). Feature -> Phase 9 unless trivially small.
design: Phase 13 scope (ADR-0079, proposed; gate-bearing). A host that abandons a failed batch has no way back: there is no discard over the socket at all. Interface: 'acetone discard' resets the workspace to HEAD's committed manifest, plus a matching daemon 'discard' verb. During a merge in progress it refuses and advises merge --abort. The merge-in-progress check MUST run under the same WriteLock as the reset. reset_workspace_to_head takes the lock itself, so a check made before calling it is a time-of-check/time-of-use gap; refactor to an inner unlocked variant called under one lock. CAS on the workspace ref. Shared workspace: under the daemon's model, one connection's discard throws away every connection's staged writes. Document this in protocol.md and test it (coordinate with acetone-d5is.2). Recommendation: checking out the current branch while dirty stays refused, since discard is the explicit verb. Tests: dirty -> discard -> status clean, via the CLI and the socket; refused mid-merge; a concurrent writer gets 'locked'; derived maps (edges_rev, indexes) equal HEAD's (Invariant 5). Update protocol.md, the Python client and the user guide.

title: protocol.md: add a Linux row to the wire-vs-process measurement
description: From the Phase 12 boundary review's measurement note: the Linux re-run gave ~6-8x (status 0.51-0.65 ms vs 3.8-4.0 ms; query 0.46-0.52 ms vs 3.8-4.3 ms) against the document's macOS ~10x/~19x. The document names its platform so it is not wrong; a Linux row sets expectations for Linux hosts (the tenant's likely platform). Re-run with the same harness (20-node repo, N=50 medians, release build, warm connection) rather than copying the demo figures, and record the machine.
design: Rebuild the undocumented harness as scripts/measure-wire-vs-process.py (stdlib Python, reuses examples/acetone_daemon_client.py): fresh 20-node repo, release binary, N=50 medians of status and a count query over one warm socket connection vs one process per op. Record a Linux row (machine named) beside the macOS one in docs/protocol.md. Docs + tooling only; no invariant touched.
acceptance_criteria: protocol.md's measurement section carries a Linux row produced by the documented harness.
notes:
